title: Rural Home Loans Escrow Waiver Loan-to-Value Limit by Occupancy and Farm Relationship
content:
On Rural Home Loans, the escrow waiver loan-to-value limit depends on the occupancy of the home and on the member's farm real estate lending, as the member's Farm Real Estate Loans records show it.

## Limit table

The limit depends on the occupancy of the home and on the member's farm real estate lending: for a second home whose owner also holds an active farm real estate loan with at least two farm principal installments paid and no farm loan late charge in the last 24 months, an installment whose remittance was returned not counting as paid, the limit is 77.5 percent; for a second home whose owner holds no farm real estate loan in that standing, it is 75 percent; for a primary residence it is the product's escrow waiver maximum loan-to-value.

| Occupancy on the loan record | Farm real estate standing | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| second home | active farm loan, 2 or more installments paid net of returns, no farm late charge in 24 months | 77.5 percent |
| second home | any other standing, or no farm loan | 75 percent |
| primary residence | any | the product's escrow waiver maximum loan-to-value |

## Records read on the Farm Real Estate Loans side

- Whether the member holds a farm real estate loan in active status.
- Farm principal installments paid in the last 24 months: principal payments booked on the farm loan, less principal payment returns booked, from the day after the same calendar day 24 months before today through today.
- Late-charge fees assessed on the farm loan in those 24 months.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical members, second homes)

- Active farm loan, three installments paid and one returned, no farm late charge: 2 paid, so the limit is 77.5 percent.
- Active farm loan, five installments paid, one farm late charge eight months ago: not in the standing, so the limit is 75 percent.
- No farm loan at all: 75 percent.
